target: AArch64 QEMU virt, one vCPU, PCI VirtIO sound with WAV backend
source: Pinned System/Sound.ZC effect section, bundled as System/SoundEffects.ZC
verified: Separate Noise(600,60,84) and Sweep(600,60,84) source probes returned 42, rejected zero durations, started tasks, and restored music.mute after task exit.
Separate WAV captures contained 24696 and 22932 nonzero 16-bit stereo samples respectively, each with peak amplitude 7000 at 44100 Hz.
A steady Sound(60) plus Sleep(600) control also returned 42 but captured about 0.32 seconds of PCM, suggesting that the duration discrepancy is not confined to the new effect tasks.
Psalmody editor, note entry, playback and Shift+Escape recovery passed with VirtIO sound; its WAV capture contained 22932 nonzero samples.
commands: QEMU_VIRT='-machine virt,accel=hvf,gic-version=3 -cpu host -smp 1 -m 1024 -device ramfb -device virtio-keyboard-device -device virtio-tablet-device -audiodev wav,id=sound0,path=build/sound-noise.wav -device virtio-sound-pci,audiodev=sound0' python3 scripts/check-compat.py --pci --probe-source-fast --probe-source tests/compat/SoundEffects.ZC --probe-source-call SoundNoiseChecks
Repeat with path=build/sound-sweep.wav and --probe-source-call SoundSweepChecks, then with path=build/sound-duration.wav and --probe-source-call SoundDurationChecks.
not_verified: The separate WAV payloads last about 0.28 and 0.26 seconds despite 600 ms requested effects; the reason and timing fidelity are not established.
Live UTM output, real Pi HDMI and headphone output, game integration, overlapping effects and exact sound characteristics are not verified.

timing_investigation.quiet: With the graphical terminal and window manager stopped, the 600 ms guest wait measured 600 ms, maximum sound-pump gap was 88 microseconds, and WAV contained about 680 ms of PCM including queued tail.
timing_investigation.desktop: With the desktop active, the same wait measured 1110 ms, a 665516 microsecond maximum sound-pump gap was observed when the Terminal task next yielded, and the WAV held about 320 ms. The identity of the code that occupied that interval remains unconfirmed.
timing_investigation.limits: Diagnostic builds were used for the pump-gap and task trace; this is evidence of delayed service rather than proof of the precise cause or live UTM/Pi behavior. No scheduling or MessageScan handoff was added.

desktop_settled.result: After a 15-second guest settling wait, a 600 ms tone measured 600 ms with a 15456 us maximum refill gap; the WAV contained 58212 nonzero stereo samples (~660 ms).
desktop_settled.limitation: This does not establish uninterrupted sound under arbitrary CPU-bound tasks or identify the startup task that caused the earlier long gap.

results: A 500 ms non-yielding task and a witness verified that the witness did not run during the busy interval.
The maximum audio refill gap was 502071 microseconds, exceeding the four-buffer 80 ms queue.
The guest submitted 40320 frames at 48000 Hz, and the QEMU WAV contained 0.84 seconds of nonzero audio.
non_yielding_worker.interpretation: The WAV records sample payload rather than proving when samples played; its continuous waveform cannot rule out a real-time underrun during the 502 ms service gap. Physical Pi and live UTM output have not been tested.

interrupt_refill_prototype.status: opt-in only; not enabled by default
interrupt_refill_prototype.design: On supported QEMU systems with real boot-time timer IRQs, a 10 ms physical-timer interrupt refills the existing VirtIO sound queue without switching guest tasks. Sound queue updates mask IRQs against re-entry; IRQ entry preserves GPR, SIMD and FP control/status. The timer respects the guest interrupt mask and stops with sound; a session reset disables the opt-in mode and stops its tone. Pi is deliberately excluded.

qemu_evidence.result: An opt-in timer probe changed A4 to A5, stopped, then restarted at E5. The guest returned 42 and the captured waveform contained sustained samples of those pitches in order; scripts/check-sound-transitions-wav.py rejected a truncated one-note negative control. The WAV capture cannot establish wall-clock silence or note-stop latency.

Tone startup submitted all four 960-frame periods before yielding. Forty start/stop cycles, blocking and nonblocking Beep, and the settled-desktop three-second non-yielding worker and ordered witness all passed; maximum busy-worker refill gap was 13151 us and captured PCM was nonzero.

After desktop settling, a three-second CPU-bound F64 worker completed and a witness ran afterward rather than during it. There were 216 timer IRQs, a 61630 us maximum refill gap against the 80000 us queue, and nonzero captured PCM. This narrow timing margin is not proof of uninterrupted audible output.

A three-second non-yielding F64 worker completed with no witness interleaving recorded; 299 timer IRQs, a 10054 us maximum refill gap, and nonzero captured PCM were observed with the desktop stopped. This version of the test did not independently assert that the witness actually ran.
Forty tone start/stop cycles passed, with interrupts observed during each tone and no further interrupts after each stop; maximum measured refill gap was 141 us.
Both blocking and nonblocking Beep paths passed with timer interrupts, stopped the tone and produced captured PCM.
Busy task and witness passed with floating-point arithmetic; 50 timer IRQs and 10060 us maximum refill gap.
No timer IRQs while masked; service resumed on unmask, and stopped after the tone.
Existing MessageScan, KeyScan, CharScan and FlushMessages no-switch, explicit Yield, and blocked MessageGet checks passed with sound timer enabled.
Noise and Sweep effect tasks passed and generated captured PCM.
Reset while timer and 440 Hz tone were active turned both off.
At least two audio timer IRQs occurred during a 120 ms MessageScan polling loop while a witness peer remained unscheduled until explicit Yield; the existing message scheduling regression also passed.

At least two audio timer IRQs occurred during a MessageScan polling loop; a peer confirmed it ran only after the scanner finished polling and yielded. The existing message scheduling regression also passed.
With no VirtIO sound device, the opt-in request returned unavailable and left the timer mode disabled.

With the timer explicitly enabled, the Psalmody editor accepted a note, performed playback, returned via Shift+Escape to a working terminal, generated 24696 nonzero stereo samples, and recorded nine audio timer IRQs.

With the desktop running after a 15-second settling wait, the CPU-bound F64 task and non-switch witness passed while the timer ran; 77 timer IRQs and a 12944 us maximum refill gap were recorded, and captured PCM was nonzero.

limits: The WAV backend does not prove real-time audible continuity.
Priming all available periods can leave queued audio after a note change or stop; its audible response latency is not yet verified.
Not yet tested on live UTM or Pi; Pi audio uses a different backend and this timer path is disabled there.
The F64 check does not exhaustively verify all SIMD registers, nested interrupt conditions or longer workloads.
One HVF run observed a 69918 us gap against an 80000 us queue; latency under host load is not yet bounded.
No timer-driven task switching or MessageScan handoff has been added.
